text.p: Pope John Paul threw his support on Friday behind moves to give embryos a legal status defending them from abortion.
"How can we forget that our era unfortunately is living through an unheard of and almost unimaginable massacre of innocent humans, which many states have upheld with laws?" he said.
The stridently anti-abortion Pope was addressing activists attending an Italian conference on the theme of "Identify and Statute of the Human Embryo".

The Pope said human life "has to be respected and treated as a person from the moment of conception. From the same moment, its rights as a human person must be recognised. First among this is the inviolable right of every innocent human to life."
The Pope told Catholics "the historic hour has arrived to take a decisive step" to recognise the rights of the unborn.
He decried what he said were attempts by pro-choice advocates to depict abortion as a right, saying the practice was "an devious crime against the most defenceless of human beings."
